7 atomic changes. A separately listed required initial investment item was removed from the chart and no longer appears anywhere in the new Item 7. Both bounds of the required equipment cost estimate increased.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. New contractual assertion of franchisor ownership of franchisee-entered CRM and Hexagon data is a material control shift.
1 atomic change. Removal of the BLK3D imager from eligible financed equipment is a clear operational change in financing scope; other financing terms remain unchanged.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Material decrease in an annual fee paid by franchisees. Material increase in the stated required equipment and software cost range.
1 atomic change. Disclosed registration class coverage for the MULTIVISTA mark changed from classes 35 and 41 to class 35, altering the scope of the mark registration described to franchisees.

4 atomic changes. Material increase in the required initial fee amount. Material change in payment timing from a single due-at-signing payment to a deferred three-installment schedule with conditional triggers.
10 atomic changes. Direct increase in the disclosed initial franchise fee. Estimated additional funds range increased.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Material change in the nature of the opening advertising obligation from franchisee spending to a fee paid to franchisor. Timing of the opening advertising payment changed from a window around opening to a point-in-time upon lease signing.

2 atomic changes. Adds a minimum 12-month operating requirement as a condition for discretionary grant of an additional outlet, a clear operational threshold. Adds a condition that the franchisee must meet Operations Manual criteria for the discretionary grant of an additional outlet, increasing franchisor control.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. The franchisee's termination right changed from 'Not Applicable' to a right to seek termination on state-law grounds, a material change in contract rights. Software accounts were added to the list of assets the franchisee must assign to the franchisor at its option upon termination, expanding franchisor rights.

2 atomic changes. The number of corporate locations in the Item 19 outlet universe changed from 3 to 4, altering the representation's population. The number of franchise locations in the Item 19 outlet universe changed from 1 to 3, altering the representation's population.
1 atomic change. Confidentiality-clause disclosure narrowed from no clauses signed to no restrictive clauses signed.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 7 atomic changes. Introduces a new multi-unit development obligation and a materially different franchise agreement possibility. Removes a provision that protected P.C. medical authority against franchisee-imposed requirements.
1 atomic change. The new version adds a clear disclosure of the management consulting services provided by clinic consultants, a disclosure-method change.
7 atomic changes. New Area Development Fee obligation is introduced, though amount is unspecified and conditional on entering an ADA. A new required fee of $1,000 is introduced.

17 atomic changes. Royalty fee changed from a fixed monthly amount to a percentage of gross revenue with floor and cap, fundamentally restructuring the economic relationship. Itemized computer system fees were replaced by a single bundled technology fee, changing the fee structure and scope of services.
23 atomic changes. Additional funds estimate increased significantly, affecting the required working capital. Introduction of a new doctor credentialing fee to the franchisor.
rows.reviewReason: The row is correct for obligation status but omits a potentially much larger fee change visible in the same evidence.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 5 atomic changes. Material upward revision of the estimated annual insurance cost range. Material upward revision of the estimated share of initial purchases required from approved suppliers, with the same denominator.

10 atomic changes. Newly disclosed capitalized amount of $315,303.02 on the Hub Note is a material principal-like figure. Newly added franchisor call right allows acceleration of the Hub Note after 7 years with 3-month notice, increasing franchisor control.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 10 atomic changes. Introduction of a new flat monthly Technology Fee fundamentally restructures how technology-related costs are charged. Introduction of a new paid Doctor Placement Program with a $3,500 placement fee.

5 atomic changes. Introduces a new contractual arrangement with development obligations and termination risk for multi-unit purchasers. Material change from no protected territory (with discretionary grant) to a conditional entitlement for multi-unit purchasers.
3 atomic changes. Introduces a new word mark to the franchisor's trademark portfolio. Adds a new representation about the absence of pending material trademark litigation.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on What the Franchisee May Sell
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Removal of a regulatory approval condition from the scope of saleable items is a clear operational change, not formatting or terminology.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 19 atomic changes. Introduces a termination right for the franchisor under the new ADA. Introduces a post-termination non-compete with a two-year duration and geographic scope.

13 atomic changes. Removal of a multi-year trend analysis is a material reduction in financial performance disclosure. The disclosed average months in operation for the PC clinic population changed with the population and period.

2 atomic changes. New Item 21 adds the franchisor's own audited financial statements for post-conversion and 2022, a disclosure coverage change. Old separately lists a balance sheet; new omits it, a disclosure-method change.
1 atomic change. Item 22 replaces the reserved Exhibit F with an Area Development Agreement, a new contract exhibit with potential economic implications.

3 atomic changes. New clause permits DaySmart Recreation fees to increase up to 5% each renewal term, introducing a potential fee escalation obligation. Monthly DaySmart software fee increased from $255 to $295, a material fee-rate change.

3 atomic changes. Removing the two conditions makes the designated accounting service obligation unconditional, a material change in franchisee obligation. New $1,000/month fee introduces a material recurring obligation.
3 atomic changes. Material change in disclosed estimated initial investment range for initial inventory. Material change in disclosed estimated initial investment range for leasehold improvements.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Introduces a material new sourcing obligation requiring use of a designated accounting service. Introduces a material new sourcing obligation requiring use of a designated insurance broker.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Introduces a new mandatory monthly fee obligation of $1,000, a material economic cost to franchisees.

7 atomic changes. Affiliate-owned growth changed from monthly percentages to a single annual YOY percentage. Affiliate-owned revenue changed from monthly figures to a single annual gross revenue amount.

1 atomic change. Adds a binding legal protection preventing franchisee acknowledgments from waiving state franchise law claims or disclaiming reliance on franchisor statements, including a supremacy clause.
3 atomic changes. New arbitration demands introduce additional litigation exposure. Material change in litigation status with dismissal and appeal.

2 atomic changes. The definition of Gross Monthly Revenue was expanded to include coupon revenue, broadening the base on which royalty and advertising fees are calculated. The fee waiver/modification language changed from a narrow 'particular circumstances' statement to a broader discretion acknowledging past waivers and future action if deemed appropriate.
5 atomic changes. Additional Funds coverage period extended from 3 months to 6-12 months. Estimated initial advertising expenses increased from $30,000-$75,000 to $60,000-$120,000.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. The franchisor's approved supplier status no longer includes the Starter Kit, a clear operational change in the approved source list.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Franchisor's disclosed access to franchisee systems expanded from troubleshooting-only to include access to MAIDVIEW data, increasing franchisor control. Franchisor's pre-opening obligation changed from supplying the Starter Kit to only supplying purchase information, altering the assistance provided.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Narrows the class of employees required to sign the noncompetition/confidentiality agreement, a clear operational change in scope. Replaces the franchisor's standard form with a franchisor-reasonably-approved form, changing the approval standard.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Adds a new non-curable default event giving the franchisor an additional cause for termination, a material change to the franchisee's termination risk.

2 atomic changes. The transfer disclosure changed from aggregate-only figures to state-specific rows, increasing the level of detail. Disclosed projected new franchised outlets for the next fiscal year decreased from 33 to 9.
1 atomic change. Dropping Illinois from the affiliate guarantee materially changes the contractual protection available to Illinois franchisees.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. The old version explicitly states the franchisee is alone responsible despite any advice from the franchisor; the new version removes the 'alone' and 'despite any advice' qualifiers, changing the clarity of the allocation of legal compliance responsibility.
3 atomic changes. Removal of a specific $1,500 initial fee is a material economic-condition change. Removal of a mandatory $10,000-$15,000 opening expenditure is a material obligation change.
1 atomic change. Introduction of a new franchisee obligation to capture customer data for marketing, a material operational and data-handling change.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 6 atomic changes. The primary offering changed from a master franchise model to a single-unit plus multi-unit development agreement model. Chatime USA was reclassified from the franchisor to an affiliate that previously offered Chatime franchises.

9 atomic changes. Removal of the master-franchise territory fee is a fundamental restructuring of the initial fee model. Initial training for up to four people changed from no charge to a $10,000 fee.
16 atomic changes. Continuing training fee row removed from Item 6. Late-payment interest formula changed from Bank of Taiwan base rate plus 4% to a 1.5% monthly cap or legal maximum.

16 atomic changes. Removal of the master territory fee reflects a fundamental restructuring of the offering. The training restaurant requirement and associated cost were removed, part of a fundamental restructuring from master franchise to single-unit franchise.

1 atomic change. The Item 9 obligation table now discloses a separate Multi-Unit Development Agreement governing site selection, pre-opening purchase/lease, and site development, whereas the prior version referenced only the Master Franchise Agreement.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 20 atomic changes. The advertising fund contribution changed from an unspecified rate to a specified 2% of gross sales, and the fund was renamed from IMF to Brand Marketing Fund. New disclosure introduces an estimated upfront technology cost of $11,500 to $18,000, which is a material new cost estimate.

12 atomic changes. Fundamental restructuring from master franchise to single-unit franchise with optional multi-unit development. The covenant is narrowed to traditional locations and now expressly excludes non-traditional or special distribution channels within the development territory.

3 atomic changes. Removal of the exclusive right from the trademark license grant is a material change in the franchisor's rights. Removal of subfranchisee trademark compliance and enforcement obligations is a material change in contractual obligations.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 7 atomic changes. New franchisor discretion to step in, charge a fee, and disclaim liability is a material change to the economic relationship. Introduction of a quantified 38-hour weekly minimum and full-time operating-manager requirement materially increases the franchisee's management obligation.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on What the Franchisee May Sell
rows.summary: 10 atomic changes. The franchisee's permitted business scope changes from a master-franchise model (operating outlets and selling franchises) to a single-restaurant model, a fundamental restructuring. Introduction of a new franchisor-discretionary obligation to participate in gift card and loyalty programs.

5 atomic changes. The reporting universe expanded from master franchise outlets to all outlets operated by the franchisor, affiliates, and their franchisees/licensees/subfranchisors, changing the basis of all outlet tables. Table 4 changed from company-owned master franchise outlets to company-owned and affiliate owned outlets, and the state reported changed from NY to CA, with a new note about three company-owned restaurants in development.

2 atomic changes. The core financial disclosure changed from three annual audited statements to a single opening audited statement, materially altering the information provided. The removal of the unaudited quarterly balance sheet eliminates a discrete disclosed financial statement.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Introduction of a new contractual arrangement allowing certain locations to sell supplemental products; changes the franchise system description.
2 atomic changes. The Development Fee amount increased by $5,000 in line with the increased Initial Franchise Fee. The mandatory initial franchise fee increased by $10,000, a material fee change.
4 atomic changes. Upfront franchise fee increased by $10,000, a material cost change. New contractual requirement to develop at least three Restaurants under a MUDA.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. The franchisor's stance on background checks changed from a non-binding recommendation to a contractual requirement, materially increasing franchisee obligations. The introduction of a defined minimum background check requirement is a new operational obligation that did not exist in the prior disclosure.
2 atomic changes. Conference fee for the first two attendees increased from $350 to $600 per year. Monthly IT fee increased from $110 to $150.
5 atomic changes. Both ends of the estimated range increased by $2,000 for the same category. Both ends of the estimated furniture and equipment range increased.
1 atomic change. Disclosed franchised outlet count for 2023 changed from 14 to 12, a factual change in the outlet universe.

2 atomic changes. The timing of the centralized system payment changes from a pre-opening monthly start to a one-time payment due with the training fee. Payment trigger for an unchanged $30,000 fee shifts from lease/purchase agreement stage to Franchise Agreement signing.

16 atomic changes. The new you-own-real-estate scenario introduces a very large land and shell cost category that the old version explicitly excluded, a fundamental change in the investment scenarios. A new Financing Costs estimate was added to the remodel scenario.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Removal of a contractual requirement to retain a second accounting firm for annual financial statements eliminates an obligation. New Item 8 imposes a mandatory obligation to use a franchisor-designated financing consultant during site selection.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Clear disclosure-method change clarifying that the listed Riverside platforms are not affiliates.

1 atomic change. The 2025 FDD adds a substantive litigation disclosure where the 2024 FDD affirmatively stated no required litigation; this is a disclosure change with limited direct economic measurement.
6 atomic changes. A new required monthly local advertising spend of $1,000 was introduced. New conditional 50% discount for later additional franchise purchase was introduced.

21 atomic changes. The audit fee obligation now expressly includes the understated royalty and interest in addition to audit cost reimbursement. The attorney's fee obligation expanded from non-compliance enforcement to prevailing-party recovery and franchisee-initiated actions.

12 atomic changes. The conversion franchise offering with a reduced initial fee was removed from the 2025 Item 7. A new mandatory certification obligation with timing and cost is introduced in the 2025 Item 7.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 24 atomic changes. Franchisor gained a broad unilateral right to change operating standards and pass compliance costs to franchisees. Removal of potential account offers and lead allocation, reducing franchisee opportunities.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. The number of affiliate-operated centers increased from two to three, a clear operational change in the system structure disclosed to prospective franchisees.

5 atomic changes. Adding business interruption insurance proceeds to Gross Revenues expands the base for royalty and related percentage-based fee calculations. The Late Reporting Fee increases from $200 to $250 per delinquent report, a material fee increase.

4 atomic changes. Both bounds of estimated architectural/engineering and project management range increased; material change to disclosed estimate. High end of estimated leasehold improvements range increased by $50,000; material change to disclosed estimate.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. The maximum evaluation fee doubled, increasing the potential cost to franchisees requesting approvals. Reported affiliate revenue from required purchases increased substantially from the prior fiscal year.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 8 atomic changes. Materially expands the required computer hardware set, including additional monitors, network equipment, TVs, and speakers, increasing franchisee capital obligations. Lower bound of the Computer and POS System estimated range increased from $15,000 to $18,000, raising the disclosed minimum investment.

3 atomic changes. New definition adds a population-based alternative to the default radius-based territory, altering the scope of territory rights. Changes franchisor's ability to require sample submission into a mandatory obligation on franchisees.

1 atomic change. Removal of a disclosed pending material litigation and TTAB proceeding, replaced by an affirmative statement that no pending material litigation exists, is a material change in the disclosed legal/economic condition of the Proprietary Marks.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. New provision limits franchisor's termination grounds by specifying that Development Agreement termination does not automatically terminate existing Franchise Agreements unless independent grounds exist, changing the termination risk profile. New provision grants franchisor an additional termination trigger linking franchise agreement termination for cause to termination of the Development Agreement and future development rights, materially shifting termination risk to the franchisee.
2 atomic changes. Geographic scope removed from Florida-specific to unspecified. Measurement period extended from 2020-2021 to 2020-2022 plus Q1 2023, and recent outlets are reported monthly.
1 atomic change. The per-additional-restaurant Multi-Unit Development Fee increased from $11,250 to $17,500, a material fee change affecting multi-unit franchisees.
2 atomic changes. New annual fee for a designated digital signage service; small but a new obligation. New mandatory use of a designated POS provider is an operational requirement change.

5 atomic changes. The disclosed fee for each subsequent restaurant under the Multi-Unit Development Agreement increased from $11,250 to $17,500. New line item and note introduce a possible cost obligation for third-party delivery fees.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. New requirement that franchisees purchase spice mix from franchisor as the only designated supplier materially expands franchisor control over a required input. New mandatory use of designated vendors for four categories materially expands franchisor control over required inputs.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Development agreement now explicitly allows the franchise agreement form for additional units to differ from the attached FDD form, while requiring the initial unit to use the attached form. Franchisor legal form changed from limited liability company to corporation, a substantive legal structure change disclosed in Item 1.
9 atomic changes. New pre-opening operational requirement of 200 paying members. New optional fee of $60,000 for presales program.

2 atomic changes. New mandatory purchase obligation from a designated affiliate shifts procurement control to the franchisor and creates a new cost; material economic change. New mandatory purchase obligation from a designated affiliate with franchisor discretion over types and amounts; material economic change.

6 atomic changes. New required fee of $15,000 to an affiliate introduced in the initial investment chart. High-end estimate for A/V equipment increased from $24,250 to $30,000, a clear operational cost change.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 8 atomic changes. Discloses specific ownership interests in affiliates that are exclusive Approved Suppliers, creating a material conflict-of-interest disclosure. Introduces a mandatory exclusive supplier for nutritional supplements.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 6 atomic changes. New mandatory equipment purchase with a stated cost of $5,500, creating a material franchisee obligation. New explicit disclaimer narrows franchisor assistance for employee hiring and training, a clear operational change.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on What the Franchisee May Sell
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Introduces a material per-day fee for selling products from non-approved suppliers, changing the economic consequence of a compliance breach.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. The prior chart affirmatively stated Not Applicable for franchisee termination, and the new chart grants a termination right under state law, a material change in disclosed contract rights and control.

10 atomic changes. Membership pricing changed from uniform to outlet-specific, with higher prices for Fort Mill and Apex, a material fee change for members. Fundamental change in the disclosure metric from individual actual figures to percentile-based averages.

1 atomic change. The Item 20 disclosure changes from stating no trademark-specific franchisee organizations exist to disclosing a franchisor-created Franchise Advisory Council, a clear disclosure-content change relevant to prospective franchisees.

4 atomic changes. In-Territory Marketing Management Fee changed from an annual recurring fee to a one-time fee, a material obligation change. Monthly tech fee increased from $355 to $425, a material fee increase.

2 atomic changes. The monthly Tech Fee increased by $70, a material fee change. The payment method for the $30,000 marketing program changed from lump sum to as incurred, altering the payment schedule.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. Adds explicit franchisor final-decision authority and unilateral update scheduling over the ohDEER website, a control shift toward the franchisor. Introduces an ongoing franchisee duty to notify the franchisor of website information changes or inaccuracies, a new compliance obligation.

2 atomic changes. Imposes a new 48-hour deadline for delivering a signed confidentiality agreement, a clear timing and execution change. Introduces a new reporting obligation to the franchisor regarding management or operational changes.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 5 atomic changes. Removal of a contractual obligation assigning employment responsibility to the franchisee. Removal of a contractual disclosure obligation that limits franchisor joint-employer liability.
1 atomic change. New disclosure of historical discounting and waiver activity was added; standard fee terms are unchanged.

2 atomic changes. Annual Conference fee changed from being charged only on non-attendance to being potentially chargeable to all with a reserved right to charge non-attendees. Brand Development Fund changed from not currently assessed to a current fee of $0 for months 1-17 and $150 per month from month 18 onward.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Franchisor/affiliate becomes designated approved supplier of retail inventory, changing the source restriction landscape.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Adds a mandatory attendance obligation at the annual system conference, a material operational obligation. Changes the contribution basis from a percentage of gross sales to a fixed monthly dollar amount, altering the fee formula.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Integration clause wording changed substantively, altering the scope of binding representations for the multi-unit agreement. Integration clause wording changed substantively, altering the scope of binding representations.
2 atomic changes. New inclusion/exclusion rule for a converted outlet in Item 19 disclosure universe. New disclosure of material differences between company-owned and franchise outlets introduced.

2 atomic changes. Disclosure method for company-owned outlet status changed from termination/non-renewal categories to closed/sold-to-franchisee categories. Table 3 now reports franchised outlets in South Carolina, which was absent from the old table.
1 atomic change. Required pre-opening customization payment increased by $10,000, a material economic cost change for the franchisee.
